moments.title: A rail yard and parking lot
moments.text: The northwest corner of Grant Park was still an Illinois Central rail yard and a parking lot. After a city lawsuit, the railroad offered the land as a donation, and Mayor Richard M. Daley planned a park on top.

moments.title: Construction begins
moments.text: Work began on a park built over a new parking garage and the commuter rail lines, which stayed in use below.

moments.title: The park opens, four years late
moments.text: Millennium Park opened with Frank Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and Jaume Plensa's Crown Fountain. Its cost had grown from a first estimate of about $150 million to roughly $475 million.

moments.title: Cloud Gate is finished
moments.text: Anish Kapoor's stainless-steel sculpture, shown unfinished at the 2004 opening, was dedicated after months of polishing hid its seams.

moments.title: Today: the Bean and the lawn
moments.text: Millennium Park is one of the city's busiest public spaces, with summer concerts at the Pritzker Pavilion and crowds photographing their reflections in Cloud Gate.

facts.label: Cost
facts.note: The Encyclopedia of Chicago gives about $475 million; other sources say $490 to $500 million.

sources.title: How Millennium Park Became "America's Most Dazzling Urban Park" (WTTW)

checked.notes: Built over the Illinois Central rail yard and a parking lot at Grant Park's northwest corner (Encyclopedia of Chicago, Millennium Park Foundation, WTTW). Construction from Oct 1998; opened July 16, 2004, four years late (Wikipedia). Cost: about $475 million (Encyclopedia of Chicago), roughly $490 million (Millennium Park Foundation) or about $500 million (ABC7), from a $150 million first estimate; the conservative figure is used. Cloud Gate dedicated May 15, 2006.
